This transmitter is mostly located in diffuse neuronal systems in the CNS, with cell bodies particularly in the raphe nuclei. It appears to play a major role in the expression of mood states, and many antidepressant drugs are thought to increase its functional activity.

A. Acetylcholine
B. Dopamine
C. GABA
D. Serotonin

Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) functions as a diffusible second messenger after activation of:

A. Acetylcholine M1 receptors
B. Beta1 adrenoceptors
C. 5-HT3 receptors
D. GABAA receptors

A 45-year-old male patient presents with muscle weakness, numbness, and decreased electrical responses to stimuli. Laboratory tests reveal hyperkalemia. What is the MAJOR reason that hyperkalemia can lead to weakened electrical responses?

A. More voltage-gated K+ gates are open
B. More voltage-gated K+ gates are closed
C. More voltage-gated Na+ channel inactivation gates are open
D. More voltage-gated Na+ channel inactivation gates are closed

Some types of seizure activity are associated with uncontrolled and increased depolarization in certain areas of the brain. Some treatments include interventions that help overexcited cells to repolarize. Ion current flow through which ion channel allows a neuron to repolarize during a normal action potential?

A. Voltage-gated Na+
B. Voltage-gated K+
C. Voltage-gated Ca2+
D. K+ leak

A 65-year-old woman presents to the neurology clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in her feet, as well as difficulty walking. These symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past few months. Clinical examination and further testing suggest a diagnosis of peripheral neuropathy with ongoing demyelination.

In the context of this patient's peripheral neuropathy and demyelinating process, which type of glial cell would most likely be undergoing degeneration?

A. Schwann cell
B. Astrocyte
C. Oligodendrocyte
D. Microglial cell

A neurologist is examining brain tissue under a microscope to better understand the structural organization of various neurons and their functional implications. She focuses on a particular neuron with a unique structure and wants to identify its characteristics that are consistent with cortical pyramidal neurons.

Which one is a characteristic typical of a cortical pyramidal neuron?

A. The likely neurotransmitter of this cell is GABA.
B. Pyramidal neuron dendrites are ensheathed by Schwann cells.
C. This cell is likely to have both local and distant axonal projections.
D. Most cortical regions contain far fewer pyramidal neurons than non-pyramidal neurons.

A 30-year-old pregnant woman is at a routine prenatal visit. She is curious about the development of her baby's nervous system. The obstetrician explains the various stages of neural development, including the role of neural crest cells. The doctor mentions a specific type of cell that is an embryological derivative of the neural crest and has a unique structural feature: a single bifurcating axon with one end in the periphery and the other in the central nervous system.

Which of the following cell types best matches the description provided by the obstetrician?

A. Betz cell
B. Dorsal root ganglion neuron
C. Sympathetic postganglionic neuron
D. Purkinje cell

A 28-year-old man comes to the physician because of sensory disturbances. MRI shows a fluid-filled cavity in the spinal canal within the lower cervical spinal cord. Neurological examination is most likely to show which of the following symptoms?

A. Reduced discriminative touch sensations in all extremities
B. Bilateral impairment of pain and temperature sensations in the upper extremities
C. Muscle weakness in the lower extremities
D. Increased deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities

A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department following a stabbing injury to his back. Neurological examination reveals weakness and loss of vibratory and proprioceptive sensation in his right leg. Additionally, there is a loss of pain and temperature sensation on the left side of the body below the level of the injury.

Which of the following best describes the deficits observed in this patient?

A. Complete transection of the spinal cord
B. Injury to the anterior part of the spinal cord
C. Hemisection of the spinal cord on the right side
D. Lesion affecting the dorsal columns bilaterally

A 48-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in her right hand, which has been worsening over the past few months. She mentions that these symptoms are particularly bothersome at night and often wake her up. She also experiences occasional pain radiating from the wrist to the forearm. On examination, there is decreased sensation over the thumb, index finger, middle finger, and the lateral half of the ring finger.

What is the most likely location of the lesion causing the patient's symptoms?

A. Cervical spinal cord
B. Median nerve at the wrist
C. Motor cortex
D. Ulnar nerve at the elbow

A pregnant patient is exposed to a teratogen during neurulation that damages neural crest cells. The development of which of the following would be most affected by this event?

A. Aortic arches
B. Bones of the face
C. Muscles of facial expression
D. Muscles of mastication

One developmental process that occurs in the head is the formation of placodes that subsequently invaginate to form various structures. Which two structures listed below develop in this manner?

A. Eustachian tube, nasal cavity
B. Olfactory epithelium, lens
C. Middle ear cavity, retina
D. Superior parathyroid gland, pupil

A 52-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of difficulty reading for the past two weeks. She reports that she can write without any problems and can understand spoken language, but she cannot comprehend written words. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. On examination, her speech is fluent and she can repeat spoken words and name objects. She can write sentences correctly but fails to read what she has just written. When testing her visual fields, she is found to have a deficit in the right half of the visual field in both eyes. An MRI of the brain is ordered.

Which of the following regions is most likely to show pathology on MRI to explain her symptoms?

A. Left angular gyrus
B. Left frontal eye field
C. Left optic radiation
D. Right optic nerve

A 29-year-old woman undergoes elective abdominal surgery. Postoperatively, she complains of persistent pain in the incision area. The patient states that she used to take only a mild analgesic for relief, but now finds herself doubling the medication for the same effect. On examination, light palpation of the surrounding skin significantly increases her pain response. The patient's medication records do not suggest an increased tolerance to analgesics.

Which of the following is the most likely explanation for her exaggerated pain response?

A. Allodynia
B. Hyperalgesia
C. Analgesia
D. Paresthesia

A 56-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and hepatitis C presents to the emergency department complaining of right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain for the past two days. He describes the pain as a constant, dull ache which occasionally intensifies. On further questioning, he also mentions feeling discomfort at his right shoulder. His vitals are stable, and physical examination reveals RUQ tenderness on palpation without rebound or guarding. There is no scleral icterus or jaundice, but hepatojugular reflux is observed. His liver enzymes are elevated.

Which of the following best explains the patient's referred pain to his right shoulder?

A. Diaphragmatic irritation
B. Biliary colic
C. Acute pancreatitis
D. Subphrenic abscess
E. Myocardial infarction

A 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of persistent headaches, which have worsened over the past 3 months. He also reports occasional nausea and difficulty concentrating at work. His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with medication. On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented but appears uncomfortable. Neurological examination reveals mild left-sided weakness and a positive right Babinski sign. An MRI of the head shows a non-enhancing, well-circumscribed mass in the right cerebral hemisphere that does not cross the midline. The mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images. A biopsy of the lesion demonstrates a diffuse infiltrating tumor with abundant fibrillary matrix and cells that have hyperchromatic, elongated nuclei.

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A. Astrocytoma
B. Glioblastoma
C. Oligodendroglioma
D. Medulloblastoma

A 52-year-old woman with a past medical history of hypertension presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of a "worst ever" headache, which she describes as a thunderclap headache. Her vital signs include a blood pressure of 220/120 mmHg, heart rate of 98 bpm, respiratory rate of 18 breaths/min, and temperature of 37.1°C (98.8°F). On physical examination, she has a stiff neck and photophobia, but no focal neurological deficits. A non-contrast CT scan of the head shows a small amount of subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Given the patient's presentation and imaging results, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A. Observation and pain management
B. Cerebral angiography
C. CT angiography of the brain
D. Antihypertensive therapy
